title: How to Grow a Mullet: Stages and Timeline
hero_alt: Back view of hair left longer at the nape than on the sides
image_plan: pexels: man mullet haircut grow out
card_text: Keep the sides tight, leave the back alone. What gets cut at each stage so a mullet grows in without a shaggy middle.
lede: To grow a mullet, keep the sides and top under control while you leave the back completely alone. The back is the only part that needs real length, so every visit along the way trims around it, never into it. Hair grows roughly half an inch a month, so from a short cut the back usually needs a few months before it reads as a mullet. How long exactly depends on where you start and how long you want the tail.
Here's how the grow-out goes stage by stage, what gets cut at each one, and how to keep the middle from looking like an overdue haircut.

blocks.heading: Cut around the back.
blocks.lead: One rule runs the whole grow-out.
paragraphs: Most mullet attempts stall the same way: everything gets long together, and for a while you just look shaggy. The fix is to treat the head as three zones from day one. The sides stay short, the top gets shaped, and the back is off limits.
Because the sides stay tight the whole time, the contrast that defines a mullet starts to show long before the back is finished. That contrast is what carries you through the middle months.

blocks.heading: From short to tail.
blocks.lead: Lengths, not dates. Everyone's hair moves at its own pace.

subsections.heading: Starting short
paragraphs: From a buzz or a short fade, the back has nothing to show yet. Keep the sides tidy and let the top and back grow. At this point it simply looks like a fresh short cut.

subsections.heading: Reaching the neck
paragraphs: Once the hair at the nape starts creeping down the neck, the shape begins to appear. The sides get faded or tapered again, the top gets some texture, and the back is cleaned only at the very edges, if at all.

subsections.heading: Over the collar
paragraphs: When the back sits on or past your collar, you have a mullet. From here the job is shaping: deciding how far the tail goes and keeping it connected to the rest of the cut.

subsections.heading: Choosing your finish
paragraphs: Some people stop at a short, subtle back. Others keep going for a real tail. You can stop at any stage once the balance looks right to you.

blocks.heading: Getting through it.
blocks.lead: Habits that keep it looking intentional.
paragraphs: The middle stage is where most grow-outs end early. A few things help:
bullets: Keep the sides tight. Short sides are what make longer hair in back look deliberate.
Don't trim the back at home. Evening it out usually costs you the length you've been waiting for.
Give the top some texture so it doesn't sit flat against a longer back.
Say you're growing a mullet every time you sit down, so the back stays untouched.

blocks.heading: Wave, curl or straight.
blocks.lead: The same plan at different speeds.
paragraphs: Wavy and curly hair tends to look like a mullet sooner, because the back bends into a shape on its own. Curly hair also shrinks as it dries, so it can take longer to show length than straight hair of the same measurement.

Straight hair needs more length before the back moves and looks finished, and in the middle stage it can lie flat against the neck. Texture on top and a clean fade on the sides do more of the work there.
If platinum is part of the plan, like the modern mullet on my style page, color is booked separately as a Color Transformation. Text me before planning both.

blocks.heading: What to book along the way.
blocks.lead: Each grow-out visit is a regular cut.

items.title: Essential Haircut
items.body: Sides faded or tapered, the top shaped, the back left alone or cleaned at the edges, and the cut finished and styled. This covers most grow-out visits.

items.title: Signature Cut
items.body: The same grow-out work plus a beard trim or line-up, a hot towel finish and straight razor detailing.

items.q: How long does it take to grow a mullet?
items.a: It depends on your starting length and how long you want the back. From a short cut, expect a few months before it reads as a mullet.

items.q: Should I cut my sides while growing a mullet?
items.a: Yes. Short sides are what make the back look like a mullet instead of a haircut that's overdue.

items.q: Can I grow a mullet with straight hair?
items.a: Yes. It needs a bit more length in back before it moves and looks finished.

items.q: What do I tell the barber?
items.a: Say you're growing a mullet and the back is off limits, then say how short you want the sides.
